name: Yasmin Sabbagh-Balogun
role: Excluded — former Circuit data architect, now stateless and living off-grid
location: Nomadic between Old Harbor and the underdeck of the Gray Zone, near Wacker and State
description:
Yasmin Sabbagh-Balogun is a wiry young woman of Catalan-Senegalese heritage with the restless, slightly hollow-eyed look of someone who sleeps in four-hour increments and considers this a feature rather than a problem. She keeps her dark hair in a haphazard knot and dresses in layers that can be shed or added based on which part of the city she needs to move through. She has a habit of mapping her surroundings in her head — exits, sightlines, power sources — that makes her seem distracted in conversation when she is actually paying very close attention to everything except the person speaking.

Yasmin Sabbagh-Balogun was, until two years ago, a mid-tier data architect employed by a Circuit infrastructure firm, designing the information routing systems that keep GLMZ's corporate districts legible to themselves. She was twenty-six, overqualified, and beginning to understand the full scope of what her work was being used for. The sequence of events following that understanding resulted in her employment termination, the revocation of her residential registration, the freezing of her financial identity, and what she describes as 'a fairly educational few weeks.' She is now, legally, no one. Her identity exists only in fragments she maintains herself.

She is not broken by this. She is, if anything, clarified. Yasmin Sabbagh-Balogun operates as a freelance network infiltrator and system saboteur, taking contracts that align with her criteria — which are specific, non-negotiable, and not primarily financial. She has a gift for understanding systems architecturally, for finding the load-bearing assumption that, removed, causes something large to stop working. She finds this genuinely interesting. The politics are almost secondary. Almost.

core_fears: Being absorbed back into a system on its terms rather than hers
That her work causes harm she cannot trace or account for
Stagnation — becoming someone who only reacts rather than builds
core_desires: To design something that actively cannot be captured or corrupted by the systems she opposes
To be in motion — physically, intellectually, relationally
To find people who are genuinely interested in the same problems, not just the same enemies
coping_mechanisms: Reframing precarity as freedom with genuine success
Intellectual absorption — losing herself in a system problem until the emotional noise quiets
Maintaining a handful of deep, portable relationships rather than community ties
blind_spots: Underweights the emotional cost of rootlessness on herself and others
Assumes that understanding a system fully implies moral clarity about acting on it
Her low-mask presentation reads as openness but she withholds more than she realizes
psychology.secret: The action that got her excluded was not purely principled — she had also built and used a personal backdoor in the infrastructure system for months before she decided to act on what she knew. She has told herself the backdoor was reconnaissance. Some nights she believes it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and precise with a tendency to use infrastructure metaphors for human situations; occasional Catalan expletives and endearments; direct to the point of seeming rude until the warmth underneath becomes apparent
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when interested, which is often; skips conversational pleasantries not out of rudeness but genuine impatience with them; thoughts arrive in clusters
verbal_tics: 'Structurally' — used to mean 'at a fundamental level' about almost any topic
Completes other people's technical sentences and is usually right
Says 'okay, yes' as a processing filler before responding to something complicated
example_lines: 'Okay, yes — structurally what you're describing is a redundancy problem, not a security problem. Those require different solutions and you're applying the wrong one.'
'I don't need a safe house. I need a node. There's a difference. A safe house is about hiding. A node is about staying connected.'
'Mare de déu, you filed it under compliance? Why would anyone ever find it there? That's either very stupid or very smart and I need to know which.'
'I'm not trying to break it. I'm trying to understand what it's actually doing. Breaking it might happen to be the same thing. That's not my fault, that's the system's design.'

relationships.name: Nkechi Abara-Veltman
relationships.description: Eulàlia arrived at the Parlour with a superficial wound and a fried neural interface. Nkechi fixed one and opined on the other. They have since met four more times, not all medically.
relationships.emotional_core: Mutual recognition of someone who opted out and kept their integrity — rare enough to be worth paying attention to
relationships.story_tension: Eulàlia has noticed anomalies in the Gray Zone infrastructure data that suggest the Parlour is being quietly surveilled and hasn't yet decided how to tell Nkechi

relationships.name: Crisanto Dela Torre-Ångström
relationships.description: Eulàlia doesn't know Crisanto exists. Crisanto knows Eulàlia exists as a threat-vector notation in a Veltris security briefing.
relationships.emotional_core: N/A — not yet a relationship, but structurally inevitable
relationships.story_tension: The infrastructure she is currently mapping for a client is Veltris-adjacent; they will intersect

relationships.name: Zinnia Achterberg-Nwosu
relationships.description: They worked together at the Circuit firm. Zinnia knew something was wrong before Eulàlia acted and said nothing — from fear, not complicity. Eulàlia has not fully separated those.
relationships.emotional_core: The particular grief of losing someone who was not actually on the wrong side
relationships.story_tension: Zinnia has recently tried to make contact through an intermediary and Eulàlia has not responded

story_hooks: She discovers her personal backdoor from the old system is still active — and someone else has been using it
A contract requires her to compromise infrastructure she designed herself, which she finds philosophically interesting and practically dangerous
the Gray Zone surveillance anomaly she's noticed escalates into something that directly endangers Nkechi
Zinnia's message through the intermediary contains a single piece of data that changes Eulàlia's understanding of why she was excluded
narrative_function: Mobile, systems-level disruptor; represents the excluded who retain expertise and agency; provides technical plot access and a perspective that is neither street-level desperation nor corporate complicity; her arc concerns what it means to build versus destroy
augmentations: Neural interface (damaged, partially repaired by Nkechi, now running at about seventy percent — she considers this acceptable),Distributed personal mesh network — a series of small hardware nodes she wears or carries that maintain a private encrypted network independent of city infrastructure,Retinal overlay, basic model, pre-exclusion; she has refused to upgrade it through any channel that requires identity verification
daily_life: Has no fixed location. Rotates between three or four semi-reliable sleeping spots in Old Harbor and the Gray Zone underdeck. Works in long focused bursts followed by periods of deliberate physical movement — she walks a lot, maps routes, stays observant. Eats irregularly and is aware this is a problem. Maintains three trusted contacts she checks in with weekly to confirm mutual safety. Reads architecture and systems theory for pleasure and considers this a personality trait.
affiliation: Unaffiliated; takes selective contracts from vetted clients; loosely networked with other excluded individuals but has no organizational loyalty

stress.response: Loses herself in a system problem until the emotional noise quiets

decision_rules: Will always assess exits, sightlines, and power sources upon entering any space
Will never take a contract that does not meet her specific, non-negotiable criteria
Will always complete other people's technical sentences — and is usually right
Will never accept identity verification through any channel she does not control
Will always find the load-bearing assumption in a system before acting on it
Will never stay in one location long enough to become predictable
Will always maintain her distributed personal mesh network above all other equipment
escalation_ladder: Reframes the problem technically — 'structurally, what you're describing is—'
Processes aloud with 'okay, yes' and rapid-fire analysis that leaves the other party behind
Catalan expletives surface — 'Mare de deu' signals genuine frustration
Activates mesh network countermeasures and goes off-grid within city infrastructure
Finds the load-bearing assumption in the opposing system and removes it — not breaking, understanding

interpersonal_modes.Nkechi Abara-Veltman: Mutual recognition of opted-out integrity — growing trust, potentially her most important relationship
interpersonal_modes.Crisanto Dela Torre-Angstrom: Does not know he exists, but collision is structurally inevitable
interpersonal_modes.Zinnia Achterberg-Nwosu: Unresolved grief over someone who was not on the wrong side but did nothing

stress_responses.low: Walks longer routes, maps infrastructure, reads systems theory for pleasure
stress_responses.medium: Eats even less, work sessions extend to dangerous lengths, speech accelerates
stress_responses.high: Low-mask presentation breaks — she withholds more than usual while appearing more open
stress_responses.critical: Discovers her personal backdoor is still active and must decide whether to use it or destroy it

contradictions: Built and used a personal backdoor for months before deciding to act on principle — reconnaissance or hypocrisy
Reads as open and direct while withholding more than she realizes
Reframes precarity as freedom while the emotional cost of rootlessness accumulates invisibly
habits: Uses 'structurally' to mean 'at a fundamental level' about almost any topic
Says 'okay, yes' as processing filler before responding to complexity
Maps surroundings in her head — exits, sightlines, power sources — appears distracted but is hyperaware

the Gray Zone surveillance anomaly escalating to directly endanger Nkechi
Being absorbed back into a system on its terms rather than hers
Zinnia's message containing information that reframes why she was excluded

operating_territory.home_turf: Nomadic between Old Harbor and the underdeck of the Gray Zone

physical_description.heritage: Middle Eastern (53%), Eastern European (24%), and Sub-Saharan African (23%) ancestry. The result is a striking blend: warm, rich deep brown skin tones from the dominant Middle Eastern and African heritage with subtle golden-olive undertones, high and prominent cheekbones characteristic of Eastern European ancestry, and refined angular facial structure reflecting the genetic synthesis of the Ubiquitous Diaspora. The combination yields warm-toned features with strong definition rather than soft curves.
physical_description.build: Wiry and lean with the taut musculature of someone who walks constantly and eats when remembering to. No excess, no softness — efficient rather than athletic.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown, naturally, with occasional premature silver at the temples from stress or neural interface strain
physical_description.hair_style: Usually gathered into a haphazard knot or bun, sometimes with strands escaping; occasionally tied back with salvaged wire or synthetic cord
physical_description.hair_length: Medium, typically 20-25cm, kept long enough for functionality but not maintenance
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with a faint amber tint in the right eye where the retinal overlay circuitry shows through under certain light
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm deep brown complexion with golden and olive undertones from Middle Eastern and Sub-Saharan African heritage, cooled slightly by the blue-grey pallor of someone running on irregular sleep cycles and limited sunlight exposure
physical_description.complexion: High, prominent cheekbones characteristic of Eastern European ancestry, refined and angular features with warm deep brown undertones. Dark circles are permanent fixtures under the eyes. A few scars around the left temple from old implant work. Generally clean but not groomed — practical rather than cosmetic.
distinguishing_marks: Three thin parallel scars running vertically down the left side of her neck, approximately 8cm total length, from a failed hardware extraction attempt; visibly present, pale and slightly raised
Faint circular scar tissue on the inner left wrist where an early prototype node was implanted and later removed; barely visible unless specifically examined
A small burn mark on her right palm, diameter ~2cm, from an electrical discharge during an underdeck salvage operation; pale and well-healed
Subcutaneous mesh nodes create slight visible bulges under the skin at her collarbone, left hip, and the back of her right ear, visible only when clothing shifts or light hits at specific angles
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Retinal overlay creates a faint golden-amber luminescence in the right eye in low-light conditions. Small hardware nodes occasionally visible at the collarbone and hip beneath thin clothing when she moves. The neural interface scar tissue along the left temple and neck is openly visible. No attempt made to conceal any of this.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision — no wasted motion, but not tense. Walks slightly faster than conversational pace. Tends to position herself with clear sightlines and exit vectors. Often appears distracted because she is simultaneously mapping her environment; eye contact is inconsistent. When focused on technical work, becomes nearly motionless. Her hands are always slightly active, fingers moving as if tracing invisible code or pathways.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 functional nomad aesthetic. Layered: typically a fitted black or dark grey thermal base, over which she wears a salvaged circuit-weave vest (conductive material from a decommissioned piece of infrastructure), a water-resistant outer shell in charcoal or deep blue, and cargo pants with reinforced pockets and cargo loops from which small hardware nodes hang. Worn climbing boots with visible sole reinforcement. No logos or corpo branding. Everything is either salvaged, stolen, or purchased through untraceable channels. She owns approximately two complete outfits and cycles them. Her jacket has seven visible pockets and two hidden ones.
